title: Graduated Health Escalation & Autoscaler Backpressure Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: define and implement a graduated health escalation protocol that coordinates health signals with autoscaler backpressure and per-route circuit breakers to preserve customer-facing SLOs during regional degradation and multi-region failovers. This ticket covers design, simulation harness, canary rollout, and an operations playbook for runbooks/alerts.

Background: the autoscaler currently reacts to naive readiness/liveness flips which causes thrashing and capacity oscillations during partial failure scenarios (e.g., network partitions, driver OOMs, kernel stalls). We observed increased 95th P99 tail latencies for latency-sensitive routes during multi-region failovers, with premature shedding of best-effort requests and inconsistent circuit-triggering across regions.

Scope: 1) define graded health states (Green / Degraded / At-Risk / Isolated) mapped to concrete telemetry thresholds; 2) implement a short-lived local derating token that signals autoscaler to slow scale-down and enable regional handoff; 3) wire health escalation to route-level circuit breakers to ensure graceful load shedding by request contract (interruptible vs non-interruptible); 4) simulation and canary plan for staged rollout.

Success metrics:
- Reduce autoscaler thrash events by >= 60% in synthetic partition tests.
- Maintain 99.5% of regional low-latency SLOs for critical routes during 15-minute degraded windows.
- Reduce customer-facing 5xx spike amplitude during failover by >= 40%.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Use time-windowed fusion of signals (tail latency spike, eviction count, kernel OOM rate) rather than single probe flip to avoid noisy toggles. This increases detection latency by up to 6–12s but prevents oscillation; acceptable given our autoscaler cooldowns.
- Introduce a local derate token that prevents scale-to-zero and slows scale-down by configurable hysteresis; increases short-term cost but preserves SLOs. We prefer this over immediate cross-region failover to reduce cascading cold-starts.
- Circuit breakers will be per-route and weighted by request contract; best-effort routes get early proportional shedding while transactional routes remain protected. This requires tagging request metadata and small SDK changes for header propagation.
- Trade-off: more complex state machine and observability surface vs. fewer outages. We accept added complexity because the platform's core value is predictable inference economics and reliable latency.

Implementation plan:
1) Define health-state thresholds and mapping document in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/SLO/Graduated+Health+Escalation (draft).
2) Implement local health-fusion service in serving runtime to emit "health-escalation" events and derate tokens (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7138).
3) Autoscaler change: honor derate tokens and add scaledown-hysteresis window parameter (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/4084).
4) Console: add per-route circuit breaker viz and operational toggle for emergency isolation (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2201).
5) Test harness: add synthetic partition and gradation scenarios to chaos suite (link to test jobs: https://ci.redwood.internal/teams/chaos/jobs/esc-protocol).
6) Run closed beta in one region -> staged multi-region canary -> global rollout.

Progress updates:
- 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with SRE, runtime, autoscaler, and console owners. Agreed on four-tier health model and initial signal set (tail latency 95/99, eviction rate, CPU steal, probe fail ratio). Action: runtime to propose fusion algorithm.
- 2026-02-27: Runtime spike prototype complete. Added 30s sliding window median + exponential smoothing for tail-latency fusion. Early results: false positive rate reduced by ~72% in noisy load tests.
- 2026-03-01: Autoscaler patch prototype accepts derate token and extends scaledown cooldown. Regression test passes for basic scenarios. Not yet wired to token TTL semantics.
- 2026-03-03: Chaos test run (network partition sim) against current master showed repeated scale-down thrash; against prototype, thrash events reduced by ~68% and 99th latency stayed within SLO for protected routes. Observability dashboard created: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/esc/health-escalation-overview.

Open questions / risks:
- SDK propagation: tagging requests with contract type requires changes to SDKs and language bindings. Risk: roll fragmentation if older SDKs are not updated. Mitigation: fall back to route-default contract at edge.
- Cost: derating increases short-term reserved capacity. Need finance sign-off if weekly spend grows > 8% in steady degraded windows. Action: add cost gating to canary.
- Complexity: state machine bugs could leave derate tokens sticky. Mitigation: derate token TTL, periodic reconciliation, and operator kill-switch.

Review feedback (notes):
- Product (Lara Simmons): "Agree with protecting p99 for transactional routes; ensure the console exposes both SLO impact and cost delta clearly in canary."
- SRE (Jordan Lee): "Add an emergency fast-evacuation mode for catastrophic regions that bypasses derate tokens to avoid running into quota limits elsewhere."
- Security (Priya Narang): "Derate token must be signed and auditable; include KMS envelope metadata in emitted events."

Canary & rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal): runtime + autoscaler flags enabled in staging cluster (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (single-region canary): protect a single non-critical customer subset and observe for 7 days; cost gating enabled.
- Phase 2 (multi-region canary): enable in two regions with cross-region warmup; run synthetic partition scenarios.
- Phase 3: global default with operator rollback window and automated abort if cost or SLO regressions exceed thresholds.

Runbook excerpt (operational play):
- Alert triggers: escalation-rate > 3s between states OR derate-token-count increase > 20% within 60s.
- Immediate actions: 1) Check health-fusion metrics; 2) if localized, flip region isolation toggle; 3) if widespread, enable emergency-evacuation mode; 4) open incident and tag with "escalation-protocol".
- Post-incident: collect fusion trace, autoscaler decisions, and route-circuit logs; create a postmortem and evaluate threshold adjustments.

Next steps:
- Finish PRs for runtime and autoscaler and start integrated e2e tests (owner: Marco).
- Add SDK header for request contract and implement server-side fallback (owner: DevX team).
- Prepare cost gating dashboard and finance sign-off agenda (owner: Product).
